title: Rules governing nature need not be those of traditional mathematics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rules governing nature need not be those of traditional mathematics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although theoretical science requires that the systems it studies follow definite rules, those rules need not be the equation-based rules of traditional mathematics; the more general rules embodied in simple computer programs are equally candidates for describing the natural world.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 1: The Foundations for a New Kind of Science

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the crucial realization that led me to develop the new kind of science in this book is that there is in fact no reason to think that systems like those we see in nature should follow only such traditional mathematical rules.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 1, “The Foundations for a New Kind of Science”; section “An Outline of Basic Ideas” (from p. 1), p. 1. Scope: rules underlying natural systems studied by the exact sciences

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch01-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.33

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim has empirical implications only after choosing model classes and domains. Existing data can compare such models in examples, but cannot resolve the unrestricted assertion about rules throughout nature.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define classes of equation-based and program-based models for selected natural systems and compare their out-of-sample fit and complexity penalties. Consistent superiority of program models would support the claim for those systems, but not establish the unrestricted principle.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The boundary between equations and programs is not mathematically sharp.

Available datasets cannot represent all natural systems.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.2
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data existence: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is an epistemic claim about what kinds of rules are admissible in exact science. Fitting a program to one natural system would illustrate the method and would leave the permission intact either way. There is no public dataset whose variables are the legitimacy of a class of descriptions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim is a permission to treat simple programs as candidate rules for nature, alongside equations. No observable would confirm that such rules 'need not' be traditional mathematics or refute that they are 'equally candidates.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any successful program model can be rewritten in mathematical language, so the contrast has no separating measurement.

Candidacy is a methodological status, not a variable with a confirming or refuting value.
